chunks: Saʿd ibn Saʿd narrated from Ḥarīz, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who said to his slave, "You are free, and your wealth belongs to me." He عليه السلام said: "He begins with the wealth before the emancipation, saying: 'Your wealth belongs to me, and you are free,' with the consent of the slave."

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: the slave whose legal consent is mentioned

ai.seo_question: How should a master phrase emancipation if he wants the slave’s wealth to transfer to him in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the proper formulation of emancipation when the master seeks to take possession of the slave’s property. It indicates that the transfer of wealth must be stated before the declaration of freedom and that this must occur with the slave’s consent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3557 - Sa'd ibn Sa'd narrated from Hariz who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man who said to his slave, "You are free, and your wealth belongs to me."
Imam (as) said: "He must begin with the wealth before granting freedom, saying, 'Your wealth belongs to me, and you are free,' with the consent of the slave."
